messages.subject: Wiener diffusion model RT predictions
parts:
Hi all,

I'm looking to generate response time predictions from a Wiener model in Stan. I'd like to prepare a plot to illustrate how well the model fits the RT data, and could use some advice on how best to go about this. Each trial has slightly different drift parameters, since the drift parameters are functions of trial-specific data. Here's my initial thought:

1) take the mean of the posterior for each parameter, and use this to calculate the drift parameters for each trial;
2) generate an RT distribution from these parameters, and take the mean of this distribution;
3) use this mean as the predicted RT for that trial.

Does this approach seem appropriate? Is there a clever way to achieve this with a couple lines in the generated quantities block? I obviously wouldn't estimate the model fit this way, but would like a fair way to illustrate it. Any advice much appreciated!

Best,
Tor

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Wiener diffusion model RT predictions
parts:
See the section on “Posterior Predictive Checks” in Bayesian Data Analysis.
You don’t want to compare means but rather entire predictive distributions of
return times to the measured return times.
